messages:
Devon (CS): heads-up — Acme reported their quantized endpoint (fp8-calib v3) has a p95 ~2x higher than their fp16 endpoint after yesterday's calibration run. They say throughput also dropped. Linking the customer trace: https://redwood.internal/traces/acc-993
Aisha (eng-runtime): ack, can you paste the exact model + config they hit? fp8-calib v3 implies new per-channel scale table.
Devon (CS): model: acme-transformer-xxl@2026-03-16, route config: weight_quant=fp8_calib_v3, routing policy: latency-prefer -> quantized, batcher max_batch=8, preferred_region=us-west-2. Repro snippet they used: ```curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"prompt":"hello","max_tokens":128,"batch_size":1}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate```
Ravi (eng-ml): quick theory: small single-request batches + newly calibrated scales can push kernel selection into a slower path (per-token dequant + fp32 accumulation) if accumulation precision is bumped. Need profiler output.
Morgan (eng-oncall): I pulled a sample profile from their trace. perf-bot attached flamegraph: cpu: low, gpu: high occupancy but low tensor-core utilization, many short kernels. Key lines: 
- kernel_dispatch: quant_dequant_unpack (20%)
- kernel_dispatch: fp32_accum_attention (26%)
- kernel_launch_overhead (15%)
- kv_cache_rebuild (12%)
Looks like we're paying for frequent dequant/pack/unpack plus KV cache thrash.
Aisha (eng-runtime): interesting — routing shows they were pinned to gpu-type A100-40GB. On that hw, our int8/fp8 fused kernels exist but only for batch>=4 with seq<=1024. With batch=1 and seq~512 we fall back to per-token dequant path.
Lena (eng-platform): checking routing logs: since yesterday we routed customer to quantized variants due to cost policy. We can add an override while we investigate.
Ravi (eng-ml): can we confirm calibration changed scale distributions? If calibration widened scales, quantized activations might need larger intermediate accumulation -> fallback to fp32 accum kernels. Ask: Devon, can Acme share serialized calib stats (min/max/scale hist) for a few layers?
Devon (CS): sent via secure share: s3://acme-prod/calib-stats/2026-03-16.json. They also included a comparison heatmap showing more outliers on layer 18-22.
Aisha (eng-runtime): I ran a local microprofile with the same stats (replay with batch=1,batch=4,batch=8). Results: 
- batch=1: token latency 230ms (fp16: 120ms)
- batch=4: token latency 95ms (fp16: 110ms)
- batch=8: token latency 70ms (fp16: 85ms)
So perf reg only for small batches; larger batches regain win. Also observed kernel table: fallback to fp32_accum_attention for many layers with high-scale-variance.
Morgan (eng-oncall): posted the debug config I used: ```/srv/run/profile --model acme-transformer-xxl --calib s3://acme-prod/... --batch 1 --seq 512 --trace kernels```
Lena (eng-platform): immediate mitigation options: 1) pin Acme's routing to fp16 for latency-sensitive routes, 2) increase batching at the API layer for that customer (batcher hints), 3) roll back fp8_calib_v3 to v2 for their tenant. Which one should we pick?
Ravi (eng-ml): in parallel we should: - add a kernel selection rule: if batch<4 prefer fp16 kernels even if quant available, - improve calibration to clamp extreme outliers or use per-channel clipping to avoid exploding scales, - add an auto-fallback when dequant overhead > X% of cycle time.
Aisha (eng-runtime): short-term: I recommend option 1 (pin to fp16) for their production latency SLA, and schedule a canary of a patched kernel selection in staging. I'll prepare a patch to batcher heuristics to prefer fused quant kernels only when predicted speedup >1.1x.
Devon (CS): customer wants ETA on fix and whether to roll back the calibration. They asked for status msg to send to their SRE.
Aisha (eng-runtime): Devon, tell them: we've identified that fp8 calibration v3 increases scale variance causing fallback to slower fp32-accum kernels for small requests. We're pinning their route to fp16 to restore latency while we ship a routing fix and improved calibration. ETA: pining now (5-10m), routing fix candidate next week, calibration improvements under investigation (2-3 weeks).
Morgan (eng-oncall): I pushed the routing pin for tenant acme -> now routing shows fp16 serving for production route. Early telemetry: p95 dropped from 220ms -> 115ms in the next 10 minutes. :thumbsup:
perf-bot: automated-note: archived follow-up task created: PERF-2389 "patch kernel selection heuristics for small batches with high scale-variance" assigned to Aisha, due 2026-03-24.
Lena (eng-platform): I'll also add a temporary policy rule to avoid quantized routing for batch_size<=1 until we have the kernel heuristic.
Ravi (eng-ml): follow-ups for eng-ml: reproduce at scale in our CI with synthetic scale outliers, prototype per-channel clipping and measure quality impact. I'll take the first pass.
Aisha (eng-runtime): I'll open a PR with the selection heuristic and perf microbench results. Also adding a short-term metric in console: percent_kernel_fallback and dequant_overhead_pct per route.
Devon (CS): sending customer message now (including the pinned fp16 note). Thanks everyone.
Morgan (eng-oncall): closing loop here but leaving thread for follow-up. If anyone sees a different regression sign, ping.
Aisha (eng-runtime): notes for postmortem: primary cause = calibration v3 increased per-channel scale variance -> kernel selection fallback for small batches; secondary cause = routing policy defaulted to quantized for latency-prefer routes without batching constraints. Mitigation = routing pin + platform policy + kernel-selection heuristic + calibration clamp.
Devon (CS): customer confirmed perf restored and are fine with the plan. :relieved:
